attempts.summary: Configured node1 as a router with routed IPv4 addresses on both its transit segments (eth1: 172.20.1.1/24 toward node2, eth2: 172.20.2.1/24 toward node3), enabled IPv4 forwarding, and gave node2/node3 addresses+routes on their ens7 links so they reach each other through node1. Made the configuration self-restoring across reboot: node1 uses a new systemd unit ([REDACTED].service) because SONiC's networking.service only auto-brings-up eth0, ignoring interfaces.d for eth1/eth2; node2 and node3 use standard /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg static configs (natively reconciled by ifupdown at boot). Verified via two independent node1 reboots and one reboot each of node2/node3 that boot_id changed each time and node2<->node3 connectivity (bidirectional ping) came back with zero manual intervention.
